pseudos.text: In the face of a painful but necessary reinvention, a leader made a difficult choice. Intuit's chief executive communicated that about 3,000 full-time roles would be eliminated. To offer sincere support, the company provided a severance package of 16 weeks' base pay plus two weeks per year of tenure for affected workers, a gesture of care for those whose trust has been disrupted.

Affected employees, colleagues deserving protection, are navigating a significant organizational change. Roughly 17% of the workforce will be cut as the tax-software company seeks to co-locate teams in strategic hubs and accelerate AI-driven product work. This painful shift, while aimed at building a stronger future, leaves many workers facing an uncertain path.

A company seeking to renew itself is undergoing a painful reinvention. As part of this business strategy, offices in Reno and Woodland Hills are winding down. This consolidation to focus energy in key locations, while a sincere effort to adapt, marks a difficult transition for the communities and staff involved.
